text:
anya: Heads up — I want to lock priorities for Dedicated capacity v2 this quarter. Main proposal: introduce 'equitable headroom' for reserved pools + an autoscale policy that favors latency SLOs for paid tiers while enabling controlled spillover for free tiers.

jordan: can you sketch the enforcement model? i.e., how headroom is tracked and reconciled across pools?

anya: idea: each reserved pool gets a soft_headroom metric (tokens/min) derived from committed throughput + buffer_pct. When usage exceeds committed + headroom, we trigger spillover to elastic pools subject to preemption priority. Headroom replenishes on windowed intervals (5m rolling)

mike: metrics we care about: tail latency p99, preemption_rate, spillover_count, and customer_cost_delta. Need dashboards for each pool + aggregated alerting for preemption > 0.5%/hr

jordan: implementation notes:
```
policy: equitable_headroom_v1
params:
  buffer_pct: 20
  window_sec: 300
  preemption_order: ['enterprise','paid','trial','free']
  spillover_limit_per_min: 10
```
we can leverage existing token-bucket code in runtime; biggest change is rate reconciliation across multi-tenant pools and atomic transfer ops.

lara: from sales: several large customers asked for guaranteed burst for Black Friday windows. They'll accept a reduced buffer if we can offer explicit burst purchase (one-off). Need a productizable contract clause and a pricing knob.

tomas: CSM concern — we must surface per-tenant burst usage in invoice + alert customers when they're approaching purchased burst. Also privacy: for private deployments, headroom calc must be local only (no control-plane leakage).

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/eq-headroom proto -> staging (build 3829)

anya: launch criteria proposal:
- end-to-end implementation in runtime + control-plane
- unit/e2e tests for preemption and spillover
- dashboards with baseline metrics + runbook
- two pilot customers on paid tier with contract for burst purchase
- documentation: config reference, migration guide, billing changes

jordan: risk list: race conditions during simultaneous spillover, billing mismatches, incorrect preemption ordering. Mitigations: 1) pessimistic locking when moving tokens; 2) billing dry-run mode for 2 weeks before invoicing; 3) canary with 5% traffic.

mike: prioritization — recommended sprint plan
- sprint 1: runtime token transfer + basic policy (jordan)
- sprint 2: control-plane reconciliation + metrics (anya + mike)
- sprint 3: billing + UI + docs (lara + tomas)

anya: asks:
- eng: estimate for sprint1/2
- sales: identify two pilot customers we can onboard this quarter
- CSM: acceptance criteria for pilot success

lara: i'll ping enterprise ops about BF customers, and propose a paid burst add-on template. sharing list by EOD Thurs.

tomas: i'll draft pilot success checklist: latency SLO met for 99% of requests, no customer-visible preemptions >2 during pilot, billing alignment ok.

jordan: estimate sprint1: 3 devs x 3 weeks. sprint2: 2 devs x 2 weeks. sprint3: 1 eng + 1 pm + docs: 2 weeks. totals aligned with capacity.

anya: thanks — i'll summarize as PRD and link here. if no objections I'll put this into roadmap and request capacity with eng-alloc for next planning.

mike: ok from product metrics side. :thumbsup:

lara: thanks — will follow up with customer outreach.

anya: ACTIONS:
- jordan: kickoff implementation ticket (ETA sprint start)
- mike: dashboard mocks by Monday
- lara: pilot customers list by Thu
- tomas: pilot checklist draft by Fri

anya: tagging eng-platform for capacity planning @eng-platform (FYI)
